history.summary: A very large 1,539 sqft 99LH 3BR at $1,222 psf, ~10% under the $1,352 district median, in a 720-unit Bedok Reservoir development backing onto the reservoir. URA resale CAGR is a strong 7.3%/yr over 129 txns, but the 2000-vintage estate carries real management, leak and noise complaints that temper the value case.
history.rating_rationale: The numbers are attractive — $1,222 psf vs $1,352 median, 7.3%/yr resale CAGR over 129 txns, a huge 1,539 sqft layout under $1.9M, and reservoir-fronting amenity. But qualitative findings are a genuine drag: residents report poor MCST management, recurring unit leaks (especially upper units), evening noise, and it being the oldest/most run-down condo in the Bedok Reservoir cluster. With Bedok Reservoir MRT a 10-min/820m walk and 26-year lease decay (~74yr remaining), the appreciation may already reflect a low base catching up rather than durable quality. Mixed signals net to Neutral.

Recurring water-leak complaints (notably upper-floor/penthouse units) and evening noise from pool/playground
Oldest, most dated development in the Bedok Reservoir cluster; 820m to MRT; ~74yr lease remaining

history.summary: Mid-floor 1,323 sqft 3BR at $1.80M ($1,361 psf) in the 720-unit, 2000-built Aquarius By The Park, 450m from Bedok Reservoir DTL. The ask sits exactly at the median of the project's own same-size prints (8 prints at 1,324 sqft since Feb-25: $1.718M–$1.855M), so this is fair value, not a discount. It's a liquid, OCR, lease-shortening estate whose same-size prices have been flat for 18 months.
history.rating_rationale: The price is right but there is no edge. The $1,361 psf ask is +0.6% vs the project's URA median and matches recent same-size prints ($1,298–1,401 psf; the Aug-26 print was $1.855M). It is only -3.5% vs the age-adjusted D16 peer median, which is too small to count as the 'cheap-vs-peers' forward signal. Positives: OCR, a deep buyer pool (720 units, 128 URA resales), a DTL MRT within walking distance, and realsmart REALSCORE 4.1 with 81.9% profitable on 783 resale pairs. That is solid downside evidence on a deep sample. But ~18% of resales lost money, same-size prices have been flat since early 2025 (1,324 sqft: $1.75–1.85M in Feb-25 vs $1.72–1.855M in 2026), and the lease is down to ~70yr (1996 start). It will be ~63–65yr at a 5–7yr exit, where the resale discount starts to steepen. The 3.07% gross yield (42 contracts) is carry, not return. The algo's 725 is carried by trailing CAGR (6.9%, backward-looking), txn volume and dev size, not by value. Fits the 'his' mandate ($1.8M, 3BR, bed band ok) as a reasonable, liquid hold, but nothing here says buy now over waiting for a softer ask. Target ~$1.70–1.72M (≈$1,290–1,300 psf, the low end of the same-size prints) before it becomes a value call.
red_flags: Remaining lease ~70yr (99yr from 1996) — ~63–65yr at exit, where leasehold decay and financing/CPF friction for buyers start to bite
Same-size (1,324 sqft) prints flat ~18 months ($1.75–1.85M in 2025 vs $1.72–1.855M in 2026) — no momentum tailwind
18% of 783 resale pairs unprofitable per realsmart — a meaningful minority for a 26-year-old project
Oldest, most dated estate in the Bedok Reservoir cluster; resident reviews cite lax MCST enforcement, noise, and leaks — ongoing sinking-fund/upgrade risk
Stack/facing unknown (no profile; 'Middle Floor' only) — can't tell whether this is a reservoir-facing stack
catalysts: Bedok Reservoir DTL station ~450m; reservoir park across the road underpins family rental and resale demand
Deep, liquid resale book (128 URA resales in the cache, 783 realsmart pairs) — exit is reliable at market
Large 3BR quantum under $1.8M in OCR — sits in the thickest buyer band for HDB upgraders
Priced -10% vs the new-launch-implied fair psf ($1,518) — resale remains the affordable alternative to D16/D18 launches

agent_evaluation.rental_assessment: URA project-level 3BR rent ~$4,600/mo on 42 contracts in 12 months (high confidence) → 3.07% gross, ~1.8% net. Steady family-tenant demand from the reservoir/DTL location; rent is carry, not a source of upside.
agent_evaluation.appreciation_assessment: The 6.9% 5yr CAGR is mostly the 2021–23 catch-up (1,324 sqft went from ~$955–1,210 psf to ~$1,350–1,400) and has since plateaued. Expect roughly the OCR baseline (~3%/yr) less some lease-decay drag as the lease drops below 65yr. No override applied; the data rate overstates the forward rate.
agent_evaluation.stack_notes: Listing says only 'Middle Floor'. No profile exists and facing isn't available from PropertyGuru. Floor tiers in the 1,324 sqft prints (01–20) show a ~$50–100 psf premium for high floors over low ones. At $1,361 psf a mid-floor unit is priced in line, not cheap. Check whether the stack faces the reservoir before offering. A reservoir-view stack would justify the ask; a pool/road-facing stack argues for ~$1.70M.
